# Self-Hosting and Deployment

Covers dimension 3 (Self-hosting). Source details in [citations.md](../citations.md).

---

## Deployment Methods

| Method | Requirements | Source |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| Docker Compose | Docker + Docker Compose | [5] |
| Podman Compose | Podman + Podman Compose | [6] |
| Standalone JAR | Java 21+ | [7] |
| Kubernetes | Helm chart | [9] |

### Docker Compose

The standard deployment method [5]:

```bash
curl -o docker-compose.yml \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kestra-io/kestra/develop/docker-compose.yml
docker compose up -d
```

- Image: `kestra/kestra:latest` [5]
- Command: `server standalone --worker-thread=128` [5]
- Default UI: `http://localhost:8080` [5]
- Default credentials: `admin@kestra.io:kestra` [17]
- Volumes: `/app/storage` (data), `/var/run/docker.sock` (Docker socket),
  `/tmp/kestra-wd` (task working directory) [5]
- PostgreSQL container included with health checks [5]

### Podman Compose

**Confirmed compatible with Fedora.** "Podman Compose works using the provided
Docker Compose file out of the box" [6].

Fedora prerequisites [6]:
```bash
sudo dnf install qemu-img qemu-system-x86 podman-gvproxy virtiofsd
```

Key differences from Docker [6]:
- Podman runs containers through a VM, requiring volume mounting to the VM
  (`-v /tmp:/tmp -v $PWD:$PWD`)
- Must initialize a rootful podman machine
- `DOCKER_HOST` environment variable may need adjustment
- Runs in root mode for development

### Standalone JAR

For non-containerized deployment [7]:

- Download from `https://api.kestra.io/v1/versions/download`
- Requires Java 21+ (runtime JDK 25 as of v1.3) [7][8]
- Local mode: `./kestra server local` (embedded H2, dev only) [7]
- Standalone mode: `./kestra server standalone` (external database) [7]
- Config: `--config path/to/application.yaml` or `KESTRA_CONFIGURATION` env
  var [7]
- Default config location: `${HOME}/.kestra/config.yaml` [7]
- Ships without plugins; install via `kestra plugins install <dir>` [7]
- Systemd unit template available (Type=simple, KillMode=mixed) [7]

## Resource Requirements

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Minimum RAM | 4 GiB | [8] |
| Minimum CPU | 2 vCPUs | [8] |
| DB connections (standalone) | 10 | [8] |
| DB connections (separated) | 40 (10 per component) | [8] |
| Docker-in-Docker | Required for script tasks | [8] |

**Note:** The 4 GiB minimum is for the Kestra process itself. A PostgreSQL
container alongside Kestra on the same host will add ~256-512 MB. Total
baseline for a Docker Compose deployment: approximately 5 GiB RAM.

---

## Database Backends

| Database | Version | Use Case | Source |
|----------|---------|----------|--------|
| PostgreSQL | 14+ | Production (recommended) | [8] |
| MySQL | 8+ (not 8.0.31) | Production | [8] |
| H2 | Embedded | Development only | [7] |

MySQL requires time zone tables to be loaded for proper scheduler function [8].

Enterprise edition additionally requires Kafka 3+ and Elasticsearch 7+ or
OpenSearch 2+ for HA deployments [8].

---

## Storage

Internal storage for execution artifacts [8]:
- MinIO 8+
- AWS S3
- Google Cloud GCS
- Azure Blob Storage
- Local filesystem (default for standalone)

---

## Single-Host Viability

Kestra is explicitly designed for single-host deployment in its standalone
mode [9]. The standalone server runs all components (scheduler, executor,
worker, webserver) in a single process with the database as the only external
dependency [9].

For a personal workstation running Fedora with Podman [6]:
1. Podman Compose is officially supported and documented
2. Uses the same Docker Compose file without modification
3. PostgreSQL container + Kestra container = ~5 GiB RAM baseline
4. No Kubernetes required

---

## Gaps and Limitations

- No published benchmarks for idle RAM consumption (4 GiB is documented
  minimum, actual idle usage not specified)
- Docker-in-Docker requirement for script tasks may complicate rootless
  container setups
- Podman documentation assumes rootful mode; rootless Podman compatibility
  not confirmed
- AWS ECS Fargate explicitly unsupported due to Docker-in-Docker requirement [8]
